text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where code changes are automatically built and tested. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, developers merge their work into a shared repository several times a day. Each time this happens, a CI pipeline starts running automated builds and a full suite of tests. The main goal is to catch issues early, long before they become big, costly problems. If a test fails, the team is alerted immediately and can fix the problem while the change is still fresh in their minds. This constant feedback loop helps keep the software stable and reduces the stress of last-minute debugging.
